tasks.short: Review marketing literature and user manuals.

steps.what: Compare marketing literature and manuals to approved claims.

loop.input: the draft and the approved claim list
loop.check: a pass mark cites an approved claim
loop.stop: stop when a sentence has no mark
loop.why_not_simpler: marketing prose does not sit in fixed fields

steps.what: Hold literature that misses a regulatory requirement.
Review the manuals against agency requirements.

tasks.design: Each sentence in the draft is marked from the approved claim list in {DOCS}. A sentence with no match is held. The regulatory affairs manager reviews the literature and the user manual against the agency requirements and signs the release. The screen does not invent an allowed claim.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manuals were read against memory of the last approved label, late in the print cycle.
tasks.enabler_now: Approved claims can be listed and compared before the manager reads.
tasks.still_hard: A claim that is implied rather than written, and a picture the list does not cover.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can see a sentence that cites a claim and still overstates it.

ambition.what: A sentence with no approved claim is held on the day the draft is filed, and the manager still decides the rest.

tasks.altitude: Unmatched sentences are held before the reading. Release waits on the manager. No new claim is created by the comparison.

reach.task: Compare a public statement to approved wording and hold the rest.
reach.learn: The match can be mechanical. The overstatement is still read here.

evidence.claim: A comparison can mark a sentence that cites no approved claim. It cannot approve new wording.
Releasing literature is the manager's signature on that version. A held sentence stays out. EU GDPR article 22 is not the issue; the risk is an unapproved product claim.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A regulatory affairs manager at a European product company. National product rules apply. A checklist does not authorise a product.

Fields: Draft id, sentence id, and approved claim id, produced by the claim list. A draft with no claim list is not compared. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the approved claim list the regulatory team already keeps.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the manager.
unknowns: Whether pictures and pack artwork are in this review.
research_questions: Is the approved claim list complete for this product?
What share of sentences are implied claims?

already_counted.description: The manager still reviews the literature.

incremental.description: The manager adds an approved claim when the label changes.

approvals.approved_version: manual version and the claim marks shown to the manager

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving is the claim marks and the hold. It disappears when there is no approved claim list and the manager reads the whole manual against the label by hand.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take part in clinical trial protocols.

steps.what: List the sections a clinical trial protocol must have.
Participate in development of the clinical trial protocol.
Record the manager's comments on the protocol.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} list shows sections this study type must contain. The regulatory affairs manager participates in the clinical trial protocol with the study team. Comments are the manager's words. The list does not write the protocol and does not set an endpoint. A missing section is a prompt, not a pass.
tasks.previous_blocker: Required sections were remembered from the last study, and comments were scattered in mail.
tasks.enabler_now: The section list for a known study type can be opened before the meeting.
tasks.still_hard: The science of the endpoint, the consent wording, and a study type the list does not know.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can see a section that is present and still the wrong study.
tasks.altitude: The meeting stays with the people who write the protocol. The list is only the headings. No endpoint is chosen by the screen.

reach.task: Sit in a protocol review and keep the clinical judgement with the clinician.
reach.learn: The headings can be listed. The protocol is not generated.

evidence.claim: A section list can show what a protocol of this type usually contains. It cannot write the protocol.
Choosing an endpoint or a consent approach is not a document check. The manager's comments stay the manager's. No screen approves the science.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A regulatory affairs manager at a European product company. National product rules apply. A checklist does not authorise a product.

Fields: Study type and required section id, produced by the protocol checklist. An unknown study type shows no list. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the protocol checklist the clinical team already keeps. The trial file is the other system named in the step.
unknowns: Who owns the scientific content of the protocol.
research_questions: Which study types have a maintained section list?
What comments are regulatory rather than clinical?

already_counted.description: The manager still joins the protocol work.
The manager still writes the comments.

incremental.description: The manager adds a section when the study type changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving is the section list for a known study type. It disappears for a new study type. The meeting and the comments stay with the manager.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Route each complaint and set the resolution deadline.
Monitor open complaint investigations against the deadline.
Accept or refuse the complaint resolution.

tasks.design: Each complaint in {WORKFLOW} gets an owner and a deadline from the rule the manager has set. The regulatory affairs manager monitors the open investigations and accepts or refuses the resolution. The screen does not close a complaint and does not name a cause. A complaint with no owner stays unrouted.
tasks.previous_blocker: Deadlines were chased in mail, and a complaint could close because nobody replied.
tasks.enabler_now: An owner and a date can be set from a rule the manager already wrote.
tasks.still_hard: A complaint that does not fit the categories, and a resolution the finding does not support.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can refuse a closure that has a date and no finding.
tasks.altitude: Routing and deadlines are set. Closure stays with the manager. No cause is written by the register.

reach.task: Route a complaint to an owner and leave the closure to a person.
reach.learn: The deadline can be configured. The acceptance cannot.

evidence.claim: A register can route a complaint and show a deadline. It cannot close the complaint or name the cause.
Closing a complaint is the manager's decision. An automatic close would be a legal effect without a person. EU GDPR article 22 applies to that outcome.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A regulatory affairs manager at a European product company. National product rules apply. A checklist does not authorise a product.

Fields: Complaint id, category, and deadline rule, produced by the complaint register. A complaint with no category is not routed. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the complaint register quality already runs.
unknowns: Which categories the manager has defined.
Which complaints must also go to an authority and by when.
research_questions: What share of complaints fit a current category?

already_counted.description: The manager still monitors open cases.
The manager still accepts the resolution.

incremental.description: The manager adds a category when complaints do not fit.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving is routing and the deadline for a known category. It disappears when the category is missing. Monitoring and acceptance stay with the manager, so the net stays modest.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set how document submissions are published.

steps.what: Record the format each agency requires for submissions.
Establish the publishing procedure for those formats.
Publish the signed procedure for hardcopy or electronic use.

tasks.design: Formats the manager has confirmed are stored in {DOCS}, including hardcopy and electronic rules. The regulatory affairs manager establishes the publishing procedure and signs it. The screen does not choose a format the agency has not stated. Publishing is that signed procedure only.
tasks.previous_blocker: Format rules lived in old cover notes, and two plants published the same dossier differently.
tasks.enabler_now: A format the agency has already stated can be stored once and reused.
tasks.still_hard: An agency that changes the electronic format without a clear notice.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can tell a convenient internal format from the one the agency will accept.
tasks.altitude: Known formats are stored. The procedure is still written and signed by the manager. Nothing is published unsigned.

reach.task: Store a required format and publish the procedure only after signature.
reach.learn: The register can hold the format. The procedure is still written here.

evidence.claim: A register can store a format an agency has stated. It cannot choose the publishing procedure.
The procedure is the manager's text and is published only as the signed version. A format the agency has not stated is not stored as required.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A regulatory affairs manager at a European product company. National product rules apply. A checklist does not authorise a product.

Fields: Agency id and format id, produced by the format register. A format with no agency source is not marked required. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the submission register the company already keeps.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the manager.
unknowns: Which agencies accept which electronic formats this year.
Whether a paper original is still mandatory.
research_questions: Which formats has the manager already confirmed?
Which plants publish outside that procedure?

already_counted.description: The manager still writes the procedure.

incremental.description: The manager updates a format when the agency notice changes.

approvals.approved_version: procedure version and the format ids it names

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving is storing confirmed formats and publishing a signed procedure. It disappears when the agency format is unknown and the manager writes the procedure from the notice.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Claims, protocol sections, and complaint deadlines can be listed. The manager still reads the manual, still sits in the protocol work, and still accepts a complaint resolution.
reach: Medical and health services managers keep a protocol and a complaint deadline with a person accepting the close.
Compliance managers compare a public claim to an approved text and hold the rest.
skills_to_grow: Hold a marketing sentence that matches no approved claim.
Accept a complaint resolution only after the finding is in the file.
role.ambitious_version: A manual claim with no approved match is held the day it is filed, and the clinical protocol is still written by the people in the room.
